Really helpful recap, thanks. Quick answers from our side: 
- We use AWS KMS for key material and prefer service accounts + signed JWTs for server-to-server where possible. Long-lived API keys are acceptable for internal batch jobs but we'd like them rotated automatically. Our security policy currently targets rotation every 90 days.
- Security would like to see SOC2 and a short network/architecture diagram showing how tokens are validated and how you integrate with KMS. Please share via Drive or a secure link.
- For the Node SDK examples, we prefer code that shows:
  * creating a signed JWT (service account private key)
  * exchanging the JWT for a short-lived Redwood token (token exchange endpoint)
  * calling the inference endpoint with the short-lived token

Alex / Marissa —

Thanks — quick technical follow-up and a suggested pattern that maps to what we typically implement for customers running in AWS with KMS: 

Recommended auth pattern (server-to-server)
1) Service account + signed JWTs as the primary identity construct. Create a Redwood service account per FinTechCo tenant.
2) Perform a token exchange endpoint: your backend signs a JWT with your private key (stored in AWS KMS/HSM). Redwood verifies signature and returns a short-lived bearer token (recommended TTL: 15m-1h).
3) Use short-lived tokens for all inference calls. For long-running batch jobs, issue scoped, short-lived API keys via the same exchange flow and rotate them automatically from your key management system.

Rotation / KMS integration - Keep the private key in AWS KMS / HSM; rotate key material on a 90-day cadence. When rotating, publish a new public key to Redwood's JWKS endpoint and perform a rolling verification window (we support multiple active keys during rotation). We can provide steps for automated rotation using Lambda or your deployment pipeline.

Node SDK sample (high level)
```
// 1) sign JWT locally with your private key (KMS signing or local key)
const jwt = signJwt({iss: 'fintechco-service-account@fintechco.com', aud: 'https://api.redwood.ai/token-exchange', exp: Math.floor(Date.now()/1000)+300});

// 2) exchange for short-lived Redwood token
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/token-exchange', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {'Content-Type':'application/json'},
  body: JSON.stringify({assertion: jwt, grant_type: 'urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer'})
});
const {access_token} = await res.json();

// 3) call inference with short-lived token
const out = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {Authorization: `Bearer ${access_token}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
  body: JSON.stringify({model: 'redwood-2.1', input: '...'}),
});
```

Routing and tenancy notes - For per-tenant isolation we recommend mapping your tenant_id to a Redwood service account and using routing headers (x-redwood-tenant, x-redwood-model-preference) to route traffic to Dedicated pools or specific model variants.

Embeddings / reranker considerations - If you plan to store embeddings in your own vector DB, issue embeddings calls with short-lived tokens and include a request-id header to tie inference logs to your traces. Redwood can also deliver embeddings to a customer-owned S3 with SSE-KMS if you need tighter control over storage. Retention defaults are 30 days unless you purchase extended retention; Legal can provide a DPA clause for storage/retention.
